text:
Thoughts
expand_more
General Textual and Methodological Disclosures
The front matter of Henry Barclay Swete’s edition (The Old Testament in Greek according to the Septuagint, Vol. I: Genesis–IV Kings, Cambridge, 1901) sets out foundational editorial policies that directly govern how the printed Greek text and apparatus entries must be evaluated
1
:
Diplomatic / Base-Text Policy:
Rather than creating an eclectic or reconstructed critical text, Swete’s edition is designed to represent the text of the single oldest and most authoritative extant uncial manuscript available for each book
2
3
.
Codex Vaticanus (B) serves as the primary base text throughout the Old Testament wherever it is extant
3
more_horiz
.
Where Codex Vaticanus has substantial lacunae—most notably in Genesis 1:1–46:28, where Codex B is completely lacking—the text of the next most complete and ancient uncial witness, Codex Alexandrinus (A), is printed as the running text
3
5
.
Apparatus Scope and Collated Uncial Witnesses:
The apparatus criticus at the foot of the page records variants from the primary uncial codices available for that corpus
3
5
:
Genesis: The running text is Codex Alexandrinus (A), collated in the apparatus against Codex Cottonianus (D) and Codex Bodleianus (E)
5
more_horiz
.
Exodus and Deuteronomy: The running text is Codex Vaticanus (B), collated against Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ambrosianus (F)
5
more_horiz
.
Orthography, Accents, and Corrections:
The text adheres strictly to the orthography of the base manuscript (including historical itacisms and scribal spelling forms)
3
more_horiz
.
Accents and breathings are supplied editorially, as the earliest uncial hands generally lack them (with the unique exception of Codex Ambrosianus [F], which exhibits accents and breathings prima manu)
11
12
.
Distinct scribal hands and corrections are noted in the apparatus (e.g., B
∗
 for the first hand, B
ab
 for ancient correctors)
5
more_horiz
.
Analysis of the 12 B001 Targets
1. B001-1: Romans 4:3 / Genesis 15:6
Status in Source: TEXT_PRESENT
7
.
Locator: Page 23 (Genesis 15:6)
7
.
Base Text Printed: Codex Alexandrinus (A) (Codex Vaticanus [B] has a lacuna across Genesis 1:1–46:28)
3
more_horiz
.
Printed Text: καὶ ἐπίστευσεν Ἀβρὰμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
7
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (the apparatus on page 23 treats variants in chapter 14:20–24 and 15:1, 7, 10, 12, with no entry occurring at verse 6)
7
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Lexical / Orthographic: The patriarch's name is spelled with a single alpha as Ἀβράμ
7
.
Syntactic: The verse opens with the coordinating conjunction καί (καὶ ἐπίστευσεν), coordinating directly with the preceding narrative, and the second clause is conjoined with καί (καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην)
7
.
Consensus: No textual divergence is recorded between the collated uncials A and D
5
7
.
2. B001-2: Romans 9:25 / Hosea 2:23
Status in Source: NOT IN THIS VOLUME (Volume I contains only Genesis through IV Kings; Hosea belongs to the prophetic corpus in Volume III)
1
.
3. B001-3: Romans 9:26 / Hosea 1:10
Status in Source: NOT IN THIS VOLUME (Hosea belongs to Volume III)
1
.
4. B001-4: Romans 10:11 / Isaiah 28:16
Status in Source: NOT IN THIS VOLUME (Isaiah belongs to Volume III)
1
.
5. B001-5: Romans 10:13 / Joel 2:32
Status in Source: NOT IN THIS VOLUME (Joel belongs to Volume III)
1
.
6. B001-6: Romans 11:34 / Isaiah 40:13
Status in Source: NOT IN THIS VOLUME (Isaiah belongs to Volume III)
1
.
7. B001-7: Romans 15:12 / Isaiah 11:10
Status in Source: NOT IN THIS VOLUME (Isaiah belongs to Volume III)
1
.
8. B001-8: 1 Corinthians 1:19 / Isaiah 29:14
Status in Source: NOT IN THIS VOLUME (Isaiah belongs to Volume III)
1
.
9. B001-9: 1 Corinthians 6:16 / Genesis 2:24
Status in Source: TEXT_PRESENT
6
.
Locator: Page 4 (Genesis 2:24)
6
.
Base Text Printed: Codex Alexandrinus (A)
5
6
.
Printed Text: ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσκολληθήσεται τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν.
6
Apparatus Entry at Target Wording:
For the verse as a whole: 24 τη γυναικι] προς την γυναικα DE
6
.
For the specific quotation clause (καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν): NONE IN THIS SOURCE
6
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Syntactic / Lexical: The final clause explicitly contains the subject numeral phrase οἱ δύο (καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν) attested unanimously across all collated uncials (A, D, E) without variation
6
.
Punctuation: The citation clause is conjoined by καί and preceded by a high point (·) after αὐτοῦ
6
.
Variant in Prior Clause: Codex Alexandrinus reads the dative phrase τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ, while Codex Cottonianus (D) and Codex Bodleianus (E) read πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα
6
.
10. B001-10: 1 Corinthians 9:9 / Deuteronomy 25:4
Status in Source: TEXT_PRESENT
10
.
Locator: Page 392 (Deuteronomy 25:4)
10
.
Base Text Printed: Codex Vaticanus (B)
5
10
.
Printed Text: Οὐ φιμώσεις βοῦν ἀλοῶντα.
10
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (the apparatus on page 392 covers 24:15–21 and 25:1, 2, 3, 5; no variation unit occurs at 25:4)
10
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Lexical: Preserves the prohibition verb φιμώσεις (Οὐ φιμώσεις)
10
.
Consensus: Supported unanimously by the collated uncial witnesses B, A, and F, with no appearance of the lexical alternative κημώσεις anywhere in this tradition
5
10
.
Punctuation & Syntax: Formatted as an independent prohibition starting with capitalized Οὐ and terminated by a period (.)
10
.
11. B001-11: 1 Corinthians 10:7 / Exodus 32:6
Status in Source: TEXT_PRESENT
8
.
Locator: Page 169 (Exodus 32:6)
8
.
Base Text Printed: Codex Vaticanus (B)
5
8
.
Printed Text: καὶ ὀρθρίσας τῇ ἐπαύριον ἀνεβίβασεν ὁλοκαυτώματα, καὶ προσήνεγκεν θυσίαν σωτηρίου· καὶ ἐκάθισεν ὁ λαὸς φαγεῖν καὶ πιεῖν, καὶ ἀνέστησαν παίζειν.
8
Apparatus Entry at Target Wording:
5–6 plurima mutila in F
8
6 ορθρισας] + ο.....F* (om ο F?) | θυ... F | πειν B* (πιειν Bab A)
8
Discriminating Textual Features:
Orthographic Variant: The first hand of Codex Vaticanus (B
∗
) wrote the itacistic form πειν, while the ancient corrector B
ab
 and Codex Alexandrinus (A) read πιειν
8
.
Witness Defect: Codex Ambrosianus (F) is noted as largely mutilated in this verse (plurima mutila in F)
8
.
Syntactic: The quotation clause contains the singular verb with collective subject ἐκάθισεν ὁ λαός governing coordinate purpose/result infinitives (φαγεῖν καὶ πιεῖν), followed by the plural verb ἀνέστησαν governing παίζειν
8
. It is preceded by a high point (·)
8
.
12. B001-12: Galatians 3:13 / Deuteronomy 21:23
Status in Source: TEXT_PRESENT
9
.
Locator: Page 386 (Deuteronomy 21:23)
9
.
Base Text Printed: Codex Vaticanus (B)
5
9
.
Printed Text: οὐ κοιμηθήσεται τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ ξύλου, ἀλλὰ ταφῇ θάψετε αὐτὸ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ, ὅτι κεκαταραμένος ὑπὸ θεοῦ πᾶς κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου· καὶ οὐ μιανεῖτε τὴν γῆν ἣν Κύριος ὁ θεός σου δίδωσίν σοι ἐν κλήρῳ.
9
Apparatus Entry at Target Wording:
23 ου κοιμ.] ουκ επικοιμ. AF | αυτο] αυτον AF | κεκατηραμενος AF | ου 2°] + μη AF | μιανειτε] μιανειται A μιανηται F
9
Discriminating Textual Features:
Orthographic / Phonological Variant: In the target clause, Codex Vaticanus (B) reads the perfect passive participle κεκαταραμένος, whereas Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ambrosianus (F) read κεκατηραμενος
9
.
Lexical / Syntactic Features:
Uses a participle form (κεκαταραμένος / κεκατηραμενος) rather than an adjective (ἐπικατάρατος)
9
.
Retention of Divine Agency: All extant uncial witnesses (B, A, F) unanimously retain the phrase ὑπὸ θεοῦ ("by God")
9
.
Syntax of Subject: The participle construction is anarthrous: πᾶς κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου (lacking the article ὁ before κρεμάμενος)
9
.
Punctuation: The causal clause is introduced by ὅτι and terminated by a high point (·) before καὶ οὐ μιανεῖτε
9
.
Would you like to examine how other Pentateuchal passages quoted in the Pauline epistles—such as Genesis 12:3 or Exodus 9:16—are witnessed in the uncials of Swete Volume I?
